findings.title: Require manage scope for top-level group mutations
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on all groups. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses requireManage() as its authorization check, so an administrator granted only read access to all groups can create groups and move existing subgroups to the top level by supplying their IDs. Check only MANAGE here and add a negative test ensuring an all-groups VIEW permission cannot authorize these writes.

findings.title: Return actual group IDs rather than authorization resource IDs
findings.body: groupResource.getId() identifies the authorization resource, not the GroupModel: AdminPermissionsSchema creates a separate resource whose name holds the group ID. Passing the resource ID to hasPermission() therefore misses the name lookup and falls back to the all-groups permission; adding that ID to the result also supplies an invalid group filter to user searches and counts. In particular, granting VIEW_MEMBERS on all groups causes the synthetic Groups resource's ID to be returned, so user searches are restricted to a nonexistent group and return no members. Resolve actual group IDs and handle the synthetic all-groups resource separately rather than treating it as a group.

findings.title: Enable group-member creation for V2 permissions
findings.body: The fallback for creating users in delegated groups still requires the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature. With only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, an administrator granted the new MANAGE_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scopes on a group cannot create a user in that group: requireManage() fails without global user-management permission, and canCreateGroupMembers() returns false before evaluating either group scope. Allow this fallback for V2 as well and test user creation with group-only permissions.
